abstract: This paper describes two significant technologies involving TCP/IP, both of which were deployed at the London Summer Olympic Games. The first is an IP multicast deployment used to distribute live video coverage of events at the London Games from event venues to the International Broadcast Centre and other locations. The second is the deployment of advanced video applications and services to multiscreen devices, a new capability that was tested and used at the games by NBC-Olympics. All network-related equipment detailed in the paper will be described in general terms throughout the paper as to where and how each component was used.

authors.bio: Harry Ryan has more than 25 years of experience in the telecommunication field. His involvement with the Olympics began with the Sydney games in 2000 and most recently the London games in 2012, where he worked as a consultant to NBC. Ryan has been an independent consultant since 1992 and has had numerous engagements in a broad range of industries including financial institutions, government agencies, as well as media and Telcommunication companies. He holds a BS degree and is currently attending Boston University in pursuit of a Master's degree in Information Technology as it relates to security.
authors.name: Harry Ryan

authors.bio: Rajesh Rajah is a solutions manager at Cisco's End-to-End IP Video solution/Videoscape. Before that, he was a solutions architect with diverse experience in end-to-end planning, design and deployment phases of SP carrier ethernet and video/IPTV engagements worldwide. Prior to focusing on IPTV/video, he was involved in designing IP NGN and MPLS-based networks for service providers in different theaters. He has been with Cisco for more than 12 years and has been a speaker at Cisco Live/Networkers, National Association of Broadcasters (NAB), SMPTE, SANOG and other forums. Rajah also holds an issued patent and has several others pending, with the US Patent office, on video, datacenters and carrier ethernet.
